title: Introduce classification-to-RBAC mapper and CMK usage telemetry
author: Elena García
description: Context: Customers asked for safer defaults when serving tenant data and clearer controls tying data classification to enforcement surfaces. This PR implements a classification-to-RBAC translation layer, per-tenant CMK usage telemetry, and a privacy-minded audit hashing option. Motivation: Reduce risk of accidental privilege escalation due to loose policy labels and provide the observability needed to enforce CMK cost/usage policies per tenant. Changes: 1) policy-engine: introduce ClassificationMapper (policy table driven) that maps incoming request classification labels (public/internal/confidential/regulatory) to RBAC v2 role tuples (data:viewer, data:processor, data:controller). Mapping is configurable per-tenant via new policy records. 2) kms-proxy: add CMK meter that tags encrypt/decrypt operations with policy_id and tenant_hash and emits telemetry events to metrics/billing. 3) audit-aggregator: add optional hashed_audit_outbound mode that applies a salted HMAC to identified PII fields before forwarding to external log sinks; controlled by a feature flag and tenant allowlist. 4) migrations: SQL migration to add classification_role_map and cmk_metering_config tables. 5) e2e + unit tests covering mapping, enforcement, and telemetry emission. Rollout: feature flag gated, canary rollout to 5% of tenants for 48 hours, follow-up full rollout after telemetry review. Backwards compatibility: default mappings maintain previous behavior for tenants without entries. Security notes: HMAC key is derived from tenant KMS material and not persisted in plaintext. See security rationale in release notes. Testing and verification: local unit tests, integration with a mocked KMS, and an e2e run against a staging tenant cohort. Related: references ENG-5123 (policy mapping) and ENG-6631 (kms telemetry).

review_comments: Marcus Liu: Can you clarify how the tenant salt is derived and rotated? Concern about long-lived HMAC keys.
Author (Elena): Tenant salt is derived via a KMS-wrapped key per tenant with automatic rotation hooks; added details in security section of docs.
Priya Sen: Telemetry contains tenant_hash and policy_id. Ensure we never emit raw tenant identifiers to external billing sinks.
Author (Elena): Telemetry includes tenant_hash (one-way) and policy_id only; added an enforcement test and filter step in kms-proxy.
Jordan Kim: Lint flagged an export in classification_mapper.go — please fix naming to avoid API surface change.
Author (Elena): Fixed export and updated tests. Ran full lint and unit suite.
Priya Sen: Request to gate hashed_audit_outbound default to off until privacy review completes.
Author (Elena): Gate default off; canary tenants opted-in for initial test.
Marcus Liu: Approve after CI green and a short privacy review note appended to release notes.
release_notes:
- Add classification-to-RBAC mapper (policy-engine) to map tenant classification labels to RBAC v2 roles.
- CMK usage telemetry added to kms-proxy for per-tenant metering.
- Optional hashed audit outbound to redact PII before external log forwarding (feature-flagged, default OFF).
- Database migrations: classification_role_map, cmk_metering_config.
Rollout: Canary at 5% for 48 hours; opt-in for hashed audit outbound. Admins should review the telemetry schema before full enablement.
notes: Privacy/Legal reviewed the hashed_audit_outbound approach on 2025-02-18 and requested audit retention alignment; changes documented in security notes.
